title: model.ts
description: The Lending records (Member, Tool, Loan, catalog entry), the condition values, the loan constants (14 days, 3 loans), the library settings (`timeZone`, default `America/New_York`), and the rules that need no storage, all counted in calendar days in the library's time zone: the due date, whether a loan is overdue, and whether a return is late. Also a tool's status and `LendingError`, which carries the HTTP status and error code for a broken rule.

title: store.ts
description: Reads and writes members, tools and loans in SQLite through `node:sqlite` (in memory by default). The schema backs up three rules even if a service misses them: a unique index on member email (DR01), a CHECK on the condition values (DR04), and a unique partial index allowing one active loan per tool (DR06). It also stores a loan's due date as a date (YYYY-MM-DD), with a CHECK on its shape. Offers `transaction()` so each check and its write happen together.

title: member-service.ts
description: Registers members: trims the name, validates and lower-cases the email, refuses a duplicate email, and returns the new member. A missing name or email is refused with a message naming it before anything is saved (the Librarian action pattern's rule R01).

title: tool-service.ts
description: The catalog: adds tools in good condition, lists them with their status, marks a tool as needing repair (with a required note, leaving any loan alone), and marks a damaged tool repaired. A missing tool name or damage note is refused with a message naming it before anything is saved (the Librarian action pattern's rule R01).

title: lending-service.ts
description: Borrowing and returning. `borrow` runs the checks in the order the [Borrow endpoint](../endpoints/E04-create-loan.md) lists, inside one transaction, and creates a loan due 14 calendar days later. `return` requires a valid condition before it changes anything (the Librarian action pattern's rule R01), refuses a second return, records the condition and note, takes a tool returned needing repair out of lending, never clears damage reported during the loan, and reports whether the return was late. Takes a clock so tests can move time, and the library's time zone (default `America/New_York`; an unknown zone is refused), in which it counts due dates and overdue loans.

title: router.ts
description:
The HTTP API on `node:http`. Matches each route, reads and parses the JSON body (one that is not a JSON object gives 400 `invalid_json`), calls the service, and turns a `LendingError` into its status with `{ error, message }`, so a refused borrow tells the caller its reason. Each librarian action answers with the record its service saved, read back as stored (the Librarian action pattern's rule R02). Unknown routes give 404 and wrong methods 405. Takes the clock and the library settings and passes the time zone to the lending service.

The body size limit (E06-R03) is `readBody` with `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (64 KB), and `sendAndClose`. A declared `Content-Length` over the limit is refused before any byte is read; a chunked or endless body is read only up to the limit, then the request is paused, so nothing past the limit is read or parsed. The 413 `body_too_large` answer is written whole with `Connection: close`, and the connection is closed a second later, so a client still sending gets the answer instead of a reset and cannot hold the connection open.

title: server.ts
description: The entry point: opens the store (`DB`, default in memory) and serves the router on `127.0.0.1` at `PORT` (default 5310), with the library's time zone from `TIME_ZONE` (default `America/New_York`), the setting TL-LEND-DR07 and TL-LEND-DR08 read dates in. An unknown time zone stops it at start-up with a message. Stops cleanly on SIGINT or SIGTERM.
